findings.title: Fallback package name for a scoped store directory without package.json is empty
findings.detail: In scanNpmStore, when a package directory under node_modules/.pnpm/<dir>/node_modules/@scope/pkg has a missing or unreadable package.json, the fallback name is computed from child.name.split("@")[0].replace("+", "/"). Because a scoped store directory name starts with "@" (e.g. "@scope+pkg@1.0.0"), child.name.split("@")[0] is "" instead of "@scope/pkg" (whereas pkgName already holds "@scope/pkg"). No scenario in the specification pins down the fallback name when package.json is missing in scanNpmStore.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN `scanNpmStore` encounters a scoped store directory `@scope+pkg@1.0.0` whose `package.json` is missing or invalid THEN it returns an entry with `name: ""`, `version: "unknown"`, `licence: null` and `terms: null`

findings.title: Fallback package name for a scoped store directory without package.json is empty
findings.detail: In scanNpmStore, when a package directory under node_modules/.pnpm/<dir>/node_modules/@scope/pkg has a missing or unreadable package.json, the fallback name is computed from child.name.split("@")[0].replace("+", "/"). Because a scoped store directory name starts with "@" (e.g. "@scope+pkg@1.0.0"), child.name.split("@")[0] is "" instead of "@scope/pkg" (whereas pkgName already holds "@scope/pkg"). No scenario in the specification pins down the fallback name when package.json is missing in scanNpmStore.

evidence.quote:
const [storeNameSegment = ""] = child.name.split("@");
